scope: One bounded 18-cell capability-surface model: three repository authority surfaces x six authority/interruption events. Inputs are current own Part122 state plus the currently exposed Chat GitHub tool contract already loaded for this invocation; no other-worker, O, downstream, scheduler, or legacy semantic state was read, and no live repository policy, credential, ref, or scheduler mutation was performed.

source_qualification.current_chat_surface_observation: The connected GitHub tool contract exposed to this invocation provides repository/file reads and searches plus create_file, update_file, and delete_file content mutations. It exposes no raw Git-ref update/delete action, no ruleset/policy mutation action, no repository deletion action, and no credential/install introspection action. Mutation calls are path-scoped content operations; update_file requires the current content blob SHA.
source_qualification.scope_note: This is a capability-surface observation for this Chat execution surface, not a claim about every credential behind GitHub or every future connector version.

surfaces.chat_file_cas_surface: Connected Chat GitHub tool surface with create/update/delete UTF-8 file operations and update_file current-blob SHA compare; raw ref, policy, repository lifecycle, and credential introspection actions are absent from the exposed contract.
surfaces.generic_contents_write_rest_surface: A direct generic GitHub REST credential with Contents(write) as characterized in Part122 public docs; Contents(write) also authorizes Git ref create/update/delete endpoints, so the credential capability is broader than the current Chat file wrapper.
surfaces.selected_repository_app_binding: A GitHub App installation token restricted to selected repository_ids and permissions no greater than the installation grant, as characterized in Part122 public docs; token lifetime is short, but provisioning/grant/rebinding authority is external to this CLEAN worker and the current Chat tool contract does not expose installation identity or grant introspection.

selected_repository_app_binding: conditional_new_installation_token_is_short_lived_and_scope_limited_but grant_or_install_rebinding_requires external authority and must be revalidated

aggregate.interpretation: The current Chat file-CAS wrapper materially improves least privilege relative to a generic Contents(write) REST credential because raw-ref, policy, and repository-lifecycle mutations are not exposed as worker actions. That removes the Part122 raw-ref capability gap for this observed execution surface. It does not prove repository incarnation continuity or credential/install binding: repository_full_name is the caller-visible binding, while repository id, installation id, granted permission set, and a non-rewindable expected incarnation are not exposed by the current tool contract.

capability_introspection_result.reason: The exposed action vocabulary is a real execution fence for worker-originated calls, but it has no credential/install introspection primitive and mutation APIs identify the repository by owner/name rather than by an externally pinned immutable repository id. A same-repository stored expected id remains rewindable with repository replacement unless the connector/platform itself pins and exposes a stable external binding.

claim_idempotency_protocol_narrowed.accepted_narrow_precondition: For worker-originated duplicate/conflict safety on the current Chat file wrapper, use stable effect id + generation/incarnation, current-blob SHA CAS for the authority object, and exact readback after success or ambiguity. Raw-ref force-rewind and policy/repository-lifecycle mutation are outside the exposed worker action surface.
claim_idempotency_protocol_narrowed.still_required_for_phase1_acceptance: An observable, already-enforced repository incarnation/credential binding that survives or rejects same-name delete/recreate and credential/install rebinding without manual/admin provisioning, protected authority, external monotonic witness, or finite quota.
claim_idempotency_protocol_narrowed.rotation_revocation: Any authentication loss, changed capability evidence, or uninspectable rebinding fails closed; never infer continued authority from a successful prior token.
claim_idempotency_protocol_narrowed.rate_limit: Treat rate-limit/transport interruption as availability only. Persist deterministic effect identity and current known CAS state; do not burn API quota as compute and do not retry in the same invocation.

observation_vs_inference.observed: Current Chat connector action schema omits raw ref, ruleset/policy, repository deletion, and credential/install introspection actions; update_file requires current content SHA. Part122 source-qualified docs establish that generic Contents(write) is broader and that GitHub App installation tokens can be repository/permission scoped and expire.
observation_vs_inference.inference: The current Chat action vocabulary is sufficient to fence worker-originated raw-ref/policy/repository-lifecycle mutations within the tested connector surface, but not sufficient to authenticate the continuity of the repository incarnation or installation grant across external delete/recreate or rebinding.
observation_vs_inference.scope_guard: No claim is made against owner/admin compromise, future connector expansion, hidden platform rebinding, or private-repository plan semantics. This leaf does not treat external administrative provisioning as solved.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.residual_richer_mode_protected_manual_ex: unresolved_for_acceptance: the current Chat surface does not expose a stable repository-id/install-id/grant binding or prove that such binding was provisioned without manual/admin authority

result.new_narrowing: The connected Chat file-operation wrapper itself is a meaningful least-privilege fence: unlike generic Contents(write) REST access, it does not expose raw Git-ref, policy, or repository-lifecycle mutation. Therefore the remaining acceptance blocker is no longer ordinary worker force-rewind capability on this surface; it is repository/credential incarnation continuity across external rebinding or same-name replacement. Selected-repository GitHub App binding is a plausible mechanism but is not Chat-natively observable or self-provisionable under the current CLEAN boundary.
result.minimal_unresolved_child: Can the connected Chat repository transport expose a stable connector-side repository incarnation and credential/installation binding (for example immutable repository_id plus installation/grant identity) that is checked on every content CAS write and survives or rejects same-name delete/recreate, with no manual/admin provisioning step, no protected authority, no external monotonic witness, and no finite monthly/trial/paid quota?

continuation: Part124: execute one bounded repository-incarnation-binding observability model using only current Chat tool contracts plus current own state. Compare owner/name-only binding, connector-side immutable repository_id pinning, and repository_id+installation/grant pinning. Test same-name delete/recreate, transfer/rename, credential rotation, connector reconnection, response loss, and rate-limit interruption. The leaf must distinguish a merely observable current id from an externally pinned expected id; if no connector-side pin is exposed, preserve that as the minimal unresolved child and do not substitute manual/admin setup. Persist one checkpoint and no second leaf.
